title: Simultaneous Multi-Project Management Protocol
purpose: Enables a central commander to run multiple independent projects simultaneously using hub-and-spoke monitoring. Covers project decomposition, team group management, cross-project resource sharing, and parallel progress tracking.

motivation.problem: Previous operations ran a single project at a time. Users often need multiple workstreams running simultaneously (e.g., indexing + bug testing + documentation). Without formal project isolation, teams from different projects interfere, share resources without coordination, and overwhelm the coordinator.
evidence: TEAM-0025 ran 14 agents across a single bugfix project successfully, demonstrating hub-and-spoke scales to 14+ agents.
TEAM-0026 infrastructure project requires 20 sub-agents across 6 think tank teams doing 3+ distinct projects simultaneously.
Prior sessions showed that without project isolation, agent outputs can collide on file paths, status entries get confused, and the coordinator loses track of which agent belongs to which project.
motivation.goal: Enable coordinators to manage 2-5 simultaneous projects, each with their own team groups, output paths, and progress tracking, all monitored from a single commander dashboard.

section_1_project_decomposition.title: Project Decomposition and Grouping
section_1_project_decomposition.description: How to break a multi-project request into isolated project groups that can run simultaneously.

step_1_identify_projects.action: Parse the user request for distinct project objectives. Each objective that produces independent deliverables is a separate project.

examples.user_request: Mass indexing, inventory, bug testing, and documentation

projects.name: Mass Indexing & Inventory
projects.objective: Create comprehensive file index and tool inventory

projects.name: Bug Testing & Fixing
projects.objective: Identify and fix bugs across all systems

projects.name: Documentation & SOP Creation
projects.objective: Create system documentation and new SOPs

step_2_assign_team_groups.action: For each project, assign a team group. Each group operates independently with its own output directory.

step_3_isolate_output_paths.action: Each project group gets its own output directory. No cross-writing allowed.

step_4_identify_cross_project_dependenci.action: Apply the Hard Dependency Test (SOP-011) across projects, not just within them.
common_false_dependencies: Documentation team doesn't need bug team's results - both can read source code directly
Indexing team doesn't need documentation team's output - both read the filesystem
Bug testing doesn't need indexing results - bug testers read code directly
common_true_dependencies: Bug fixing team needs bug testing team's report before it can fix bugs
Documentation updates need bug fixes applied first to document correct behavior

section_2_central_commander_protocol.title: Central Commander Protocol for Multi-Project Operations
section_2_central_commander_protocol.description: The coordinator acts as central commander, maintaining visibility across all projects without micromanaging individual teams.
commander_responsibilities: Deploy all project groups simultaneously (per SOP-011 anti-sequential rules)
Monitor progress across all projects using hub dashboard
Detect cross-project conflicts (resource contention, file collisions)
Redistribute resources when one project finishes early
Aggregate final outputs across all projects into unified deliverables

dashboard_view.description: The commander should maintain a mental model of project-level progress, not agent-level details.

project_health_indicators.GREEN: All agents in project group progressing, no blockers
project_health_indicators.YELLOW: One agent stalled or behind, others progressing
project_health_indicators.RED: Multiple agents blocked, project may not complete

check_rhythm.CP-1_post_launch: Verify all 6 teams started (30-60s after launch)
check_rhythm.CP-2_early_progress: Verify all projects making progress (5-10 min)
check_rhythm.CP-3_mid_session: Cross-project progress comparison, resource rebalancing opportunity
check_rhythm.CP-4_first_completion: First project group finishes - reassign agents to lagging projects

resource_rebalancing.trigger: One project group finishes while another has significant remaining work
resource_rebalancing.action: Deploy completed group's agents as reinforcements to the lagging project
constraints: Only reassign if the lagging project's remaining work is decomposable
Provide reassigned agents with full context (what's been done, what remains, where to write)
Update output path assignments to prevent collisions

section_3_scaling_guidelines.title: Scaling Guidelines for Large Operations
section_3_scaling_guidelines.description: Rules for determining optimal team sizes and project groupings for operations with 10-30 sub-agents.

small.coordinator_overhead: Low. Direct monitoring of each agent feasible.

medium.coordinator_overhead: Moderate. Monitor at team level, not agent level.

large.coordinator_overhead: High. Monitor at project level. Use project leads (senior agents) for team-level oversight.

diminishing_returns_warning.description: Beyond 10 teams, coordination overhead increases non-linearly. Prefer fewer, larger teams over many small teams at this scale.
diminishing_returns_warning.mitigation: Use project leads - one agent per project group that coordinates its own sub-agents, reducing coordinator's span of control.

file_assignment_rules.principle: No two agents from different project groups should write to the same file.
file_assignment_rules.enforcement: Commander creates a master file allocation table before launch.
file_assignment_rules.exception: Append-only JSONL files (status, findings) can accept concurrent writers safely.

checklist.check: User request decomposed into distinct projects with clear boundaries
Each project has a team group with assigned agents
Output paths are unique across ALL projects (no cross-project collisions)
Cross-project dependencies identified and documented (should be near zero)
All teams launched in a single message (per SOP-011 ASR-006)
Commander has project-level health dashboard ready
Resource rebalancing plan defined for early finishers
Each agent prompt includes project group ID for status tracking
Consolidation strategy defined for merging cross-project outputs

section_5_post_operation_consolidation.title: Cross-Project Result Consolidation
section_5_post_operation_consolidation.description: After all projects complete, the commander must merge outputs into unified deliverables.

consolidation_steps.action: Verify all project groups reported complete
consolidation_steps.method: Check each project group's output files exist and are non-empty
Look for bugs found by both the indexing and bug-testing projects. Deduplicate. Flag contradictions.
Combine file indexes, tool inventories, and documentation into unified reference documents
Execute full test suite to verify bug fixes don't break other systems
One KB entry per project summarizing findings, one master KB entry for the overall operation
Document the full operation including team assignments, timelines, findings, and lessons learned

quick_reference.one_sentence: Decompose into isolated projects, assign non-overlapping team groups, launch all simultaneously, monitor at project level, rebalance resources as projects complete, consolidate outputs.
key_rules: ALL project groups launch in ONE message - never sequence projects
Each project group gets isolated output paths - no cross-writing
Monitor at project level, not agent level, for operations >10 agents
Rebalance agents from completed projects to lagging ones
Cross-project dependencies should be near zero - if not, reconsider your decomposition

historical_benchmarks.TEAM-0025: 14 agents, 1 project, 38 bugs fixed, 263 tests passing
historical_benchmarks.TEAM-0026: 20 agents, 3 project groups, simultaneous indexing + bug testing + documentation
